So besu and Nethermind... ? to reduce the complexity of the code I am for the original behaviour I am for the original behaviour too Great, please thumb up https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/3566 then, and hopefully we can get this fixed and running before the next ACD Commenting here for the benefit of those who don't read the EIP. This is a behavior change relative to legacy behavior. It reduces the effectiveness of the miner gas throttle by half. I don't particularly care one way or another about how strong the miner throttle is, but we shouldn't be changing it as a side effect. I think a good question to ask is, if someone would have proposed changing to `/1024` to `/2048` in Berlin, would everyone have been for it? If not then we should not do this. If we want to maintain existing behavior without touching that code too heavily, then we should change the `/1024` to `/512`. Already commented on your comment -- it's not, it's basically no change at all, aside from marginal rounding errors I think you've just miscalculated it. The factors even out (but I admit I had to generate the test-table to be certain myself 🙂 ) Do you disagree that the current thing miners control is throughput (perhaps your perspective is that the thing the miners control is the limit)? Currently, miners control both the gas throughput of Ethereum **and** the maximum gas allowed in a single block. With the introduction of 1559, we need to double or half the rate at which miners can change *one of* those two things. The EIP as published right now doubles the rate at which miners can increase the maximum block size, while retaining the rate at which miners can adjust Ethereum's gas throughput. The EIP with the changes you have proposed I believe will leave the rate at which miners can change the maximum block size the same, while halving the rate at which they can change the chain's throughput. The more I think about it, the less I care *which* of these two variables we change. I do want to make sure we are making an intentional choice between them though. The EIP as published right now makes it so that if the parent `gasLimit` is `40000000`, then the next block can bump it to `40039063`. With the changes I proposed, they can bump it to `40039061` Hmm... that doesn't make sense to me. The `<=` to `<` change I get and agree with. It is the change of `gas_target` to `block.gas_limit` that makes me question that. 🤔 Previously they could bump `(gasLimit/2)` by a factor of `/1024`, but it was the taken `x2` to make up the gasLimit. Now they can bump `gasLimit/1024`, but it's directly the gasLimit, not the target They could bump the thing which was half the gaslimit, now they bump it directly 🤔 (I think I am starting to get it... wheels are turning ⚙️) OK, I believe you! Would still be nice to get an official answer to the question of which behavior we want to change (throughput or block size). Yeah I haven't been able to formulate it in words very well, hence why I've been trying to examplify with testcases instead 🙂 `assert((a < b) == (a/2 < b/2) == (a*2 < b*2))` Yeah, once you get it already, intuitively that makes sense, but it doesn't help when explaining to someone who hasn't internalized it yet 🙂 Unrelated to your PR then, do you have thoughts on whether we should be changing the rate at which miners can change the block size, or the rate at which miners can change the throughput? I don't have an opinion, really, I think Why did we introduced the first change: "1. Checks based on limit, not target 2. Checks use <,> rather than <=, >="? Is it because of the mentioned asymmetry? The `<` vs `<=` I think was just an accident. I think the first change was more or less accidental aswell (as in, I don't think there was an intention in 1559 to change it, just the py ref implementation happened to do that) I also assume this was an accident I guess we are waiting until these EIP changes get merged and then we can launch Geth again with the "new" consensus for 1559? I've updated the geth base PR, but the txpool PR needs a rebase, then the miner PR needs a rebase. And besu needs an update aswell There is a PR for Besu and the tests are ok. I am waiting for your PR to be merged to update the node I think the geth code is kind of ready to start up again, but let's wait until the EIP is officially updated You may want to ping some of the authors in here. That EIP has really struggled historically with getting timely reviews.
